I was a believer, until the disclaimer. 😔

When we had a 40 year mortgage the rates were higher than a 30 year. It almost never made sense to take the 40 year because of the slow equity build up vs the minimal lower payment - often times the payment difference was under $100. Not to mention, they would have to change the law to even offer a 50 year.

I think the big thing is that the mortgage practically doesn’t pay down principal at all. $500k loan on a 30 year at 6% pays down $21k in 5 years and barely $5k for the 50 year.

I get the appreciation argument, but the math makes it significantly worse for the homeowner in the short term.

If you can’t afford a 30 yr you can’t really afford a 50 year. A 50 year is really only good for the banks as saving 200/month isnt a lot when adding 20more years of interest.  It’s true most people don’t stay for 30 years.  But we won’t see house appreciation like we have ever again probably.  So they are taking a huge risk that they pay all that additional interest and the home prices don’t appreciate enough for the purchase to be worthwhile.  And if/when they refinance- going to take a long time to get enough equity.. then their interest payments start over at year 1 again.  Can it work for some, probably, but they can also probably afford a 30 yr.  To begin with.
